description: Render the scene server-side (real WebGL, headless) and return screenshot image(s) — your EYES on the scene. Use it after apply_ops batches and after probe_framing, and judge each image as a photographer and a web designer would: one clear subject, on a third (for a page's own camera, the whole card at a readable angle); the horizon off the middle; the eye at a standing height; text legible and on even margins; a way out in view; the colours serving the brief (one accent, on the primary action); nothing floating, clipped or overlapping. Beside each image comes `composition`, read from its own pixels: tonalRange (p5 to p95 of lightness; under 0.35 is flat), clipping (share blown to white, crushed to black), key (low, mid, high), a 3x3 thirds grid of lightness and detail with the busiest and brightest cells, the hues on screen by share, and findings in sentences. Fix with apply_ops. At most 2 screenshot→fix rounds per request, then report. views (max 4, default = the visitor's entry view): pass "page:<pageIdOrSlug>" to frame one page/neighborhood, or {position:[x,y,z], target:[x,y,z], fov?} for an exact camera. Rendering is real but slow: ~10 s for a simple scene, 45 s per view by default (timeoutSeconds up to 180 for a big textured scene). The default is ONE view at 640 px; larger shots and several views are what timed out, so ask for one view at a time. A call answers within about 85 s either way: the image, or "still rendering, retry in N s"; then call again with the SAME arguments after N s and the image comes from the cache at no extra cost. A timeout comes back as an error naming it, never as an empty image; repeat shots of an unchanged scene at the same size are cached, instant and free; only a fresh render counts against the daily budget, and each reply says shotsLeft. If it returns a busy/unavailable error, keep building and retry once later — do not loop on it.

atSeconds.description: Seconds into the scene's animation the shot is taken at (0-600, default 0 = frame one). Every track and motion-path rider is frozen at that time, so a door with a 4 s swing is verified mid-swing at 2 and a rider on a 12 s loop at u=0.5 at 6. Cached per time.

maxDim.description: Longest side of the image in pixels, 64-1920 (default 640; height is 0.625x). 640 reads captions and renders inside the time limit; larger often does not.

timeoutSeconds.description: Per-view render budget in seconds, clamped 10-180 (default 45). Raise it for a big or texture-heavy scene instead of retrying a timeout at the same budget.

views.description: Camera views to capture. Omit for the visitor's entry view.

name: get_scene_screenshot
title: Screenshot a 3dCMS scene
